assumptions: Technical failures means attempts with failure category 'technical'.

facts.text: Kestrel Bank had the most technical failures in September 2026: 2,776 of 8,322 in total (33.4%). Meridian Bank had 1,965 (23.6%), Northstar Bank 1,806 (21.7%) and Saffron Bank 1,775 (21.3%).
Kestrel's technical failures were 2.94% of its 94,315 attempts, versus 2.14% for Meridian, 2.20% for Northstar and 2.09% for Saffron. Kestrel is highest on rate as well as on count.
Kestrel's daily success rate was steady around a median of 89.87% for the month, then fell to 78.03% on 18 Sep, its lowest day. The anomaly window is 17-18 Sep.

The hourly timeline shows a problem on Kestrel card payments (debit card, credit card, card EMI) from 2026-09-17 10:00 to 2026-09-18 22:00, a span of 36 hours. The worst hour was 2026-09-18 02:00, at a 36.36% success rate against a 86.87% reference rate.
The outage window had 2,229 affected attempts and about 716 excess failed attempts compared with the reference rate.

During 17-18 Sep, success rates on Kestrel fell sharply for debit card (86.42% to 56.31%, down 30.11pp), credit card (88.64% to 59.94%, down 28.71pp) and card EMI (80.67% to 56.80%, down 23.87pp). UPI, wallet and netbanking showed no significant change.

On Kestrel card payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the 17-18 Sep window versus 22 in the baseline window). Other failure codes were flat or lower.

response.headline: Kestrel Bank had the most technical payment failures in September (2,776, or 33.4% of all technical failures). Most of the damage came from a 36-hour card outage from 10:00 on 17 Sep to 22:00 on 18 Sep.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Kestrel Bank for its incident log for 17-18 Sep and compare the start and end times with 10:00 on 17 Sep and 22:00 on 18 Sep.
hypotheses.rationale: Failures were confined to Kestrel's card methods, UPI and wallet were unaffected, and the shift was almost entirely in the ACQ_TIMEOUT code, which points to the acquirer not responding.
hypotheses.text: A card-processing or connectivity problem at Kestrel Bank's acquiring side caused the 17-18 Sep card outage.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A card-processing or connectivity problem at Kestrel Bank's acquiring side caused the 17-18 Sep card outage.
recommendations.rationale: This single 36-hour window explains most of Kestrel's lead in technical failures and the dip in its daily success rate.
recommendations.text: Raise the 17-18 Sep incident with Kestrel Bank and request a root-cause report covering their card-processing path.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The hourly timeline shows a problem on Kestrel card payments (debit card, credit card, card EMI) from 2026-09-17 10:00 to 2026-09-18 22:00, a span of 36 hours.
recommendations.rationale: The outage ran 36 hours with about 716 excess failures; faster detection and rerouting would limit that impact.
recommendations.text: Set up an alert on Kestrel card-method success rate and ACQ_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts, and evaluate routing card traffic to another acquirer when it trips.
